Definition: to address by an additional name; hence, to eulogize
BiblicalUsage: Kanah is to give a name — to address a man by an added name, to surname him, and so to honour or to flatter. Isaiah says one shall call himself by the name of Jacob and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD and surname himself by the name of Israel; and Elihu says he will not give flattering titles unto man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe names are not flattery: God surnames His people Israel, and that is honour, but Elihu will not flatter a man with titles, because flattery is a lie dressed as honour. A name from God is honour; a title from man is only flattery.
